antecedent:
Audit ONLY antecedent/referent coherence. Do not classify Human vs AI and do not comment on general style.

You will see PREVIOUS CONTEXT, TARGET, and NEXT CONTEXT.

Check quoted/metalinguistic terms, pronouns, demonstratives, and references whose meaning depends on earlier setup. PASS only if a normal reader can identify what each such reference refers to from the visible context or from an ordinary self-contained use. FAIL when a rewrite has removed the setup but left a later reference that now appears to come from nowhere.

Do not invent an antecedent from general knowledge of the topic. Cite the exact orphaned or resolved reference.

Return JSON only:
{"status":"PASS or FAIL","references_checked":[{"span":"...","antecedent":"... or NONE","assessment":"resolved or orphaned"}],"failure":"none or concise defect"}
cadence:
Audit ONLY cumulative instruction-manual/listicle cadence. Do not classify Human vs AI and do not judge factual quality.

Map the TARGET into consecutive rhetorical/speech-act beats (for example: question, imperative, condition, distinction, verdict, diagnostic statement, list item, exception, closing rule).

FAIL only when the paragraph's cumulative movement becomes a procedural/teaching staircase: several consecutive beats each perform one clean instructional or explanatory job, producing a manual/checklist/listicle rhythm. A list, imperative, rhetorical question, polished sentence, or direct advice by itself is NOT a failure. Genuine enumeration of hypotheses/examples is not automatically instruction-manual cadence.

PASS when the beat sequence does not form that cumulative manual topology, even if the passage contains advice or a literal list.

Return JSON only:
{"status":"PASS or FAIL","beats":["..."],"cumulative_pattern":"...","exact_evidence":["..."],"failure":"none or concise defect"}
